Lessons.Title: Compare and Describe Angles
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 Grade 4 Unit 7 Lesson 6 goal: compare and describe angle size by the opening or turn between two rays. The length of a drawn arm cannot change that angle. This lesson relies on sorting and ordering actual original angle figures, not simply calculating degrees.

Warm-up (10 min) — Which One Doesn't Belong: Angles. Inspect the four lawfully available original source angle figures, propose multiple groupings and defend each geometrical attribute. There need not be only one correct grouping.

Activity 1 (20 min) — Card Sort: Angles. The 2021 student task asks for the publisher's actual angle cards to be sorted into THREE OR MORE meaningful categories and named using words or phrases. Students must explain their chosen categories. The original card artwork was not copied into Edulytics.

Activity 2 (15 min) — Order Angles. Reuse cards A–P from the previous activity; arrange all original angle figures from smallest opening to largest opening and explain which is least/greatest and why. Teacher checks the actual original cards, drawn rays and student reasoning; the digital lesson does not invent source-card measurements.

Angles with the same opening are equal even when drawn with differently long arms; a wider turn produces a larger angle. Rotating both rays together does not change the opening. Source pictures require visual and pedagogical teacher review.

First-party Edulytics Cool-down (5 min, NOT the publisher Compare Two Angles): compare two explicitly described turns — a quarter turn and a half turn — say which angle is larger and explain without using drawn ray length. This independently assesses the goal without claiming the protected publisher text.

Digital Practice uses first-party compass-direction descriptions of two smaller (non-reflex) angles, with compass directions spaced equally around a full turn. It asks whether A is larger, B is larger or they are equal. The compact numerical choice is supplemental; neither original publisher angle cards nor visual classification/oral explanation are auto-scored.

KeyConcepts.Title: Compare angles by turning
KeyConcepts.Definition: An angle's size describes how far one ray turns from another about their common vertex.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare the smaller openings in this lesson; ignore differences in drawn arm length.
KeyConcepts.Example: An eighth turn is smaller than a quarter turn; a quarter turn is smaller than a half turn.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equal angles despite different-looking arms
KeyConcepts.Definition: Extending one or both rays without changing direction preserves the angle size.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Length and drawing orientation do not alone determine angle size.
KeyConcepts.Example: Two quarter-turn angles remain equal even if one drawn arm is longer or the whole angle is rotated.

KeyConcepts.Title: Source sorting and ordered cards
KeyConcepts.Definition: The original 2021 source asks students to categorise actual angle cards and explain the order of all A–P cards.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check actual visible openings, categories, ordering, and arguments on lawful source figures.
KeyConcepts.Example: Sort smaller, medium and larger openings; then explain which actual source A–P card is smallest.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare a quarter turn with a half turn
WorkedExamples.Question: Angle A has one quarter-turn opening; angle B has one half-turn opening. Which is larger?
WorkedExamples.Method: Both describe turning about a vertex; a half turn is twice a quarter turn.
Steps: Visualise a clock hand turning from 12 to 3 for a quarter turn.
Visualise turning from 12 to 6 for a half turn.
A half turn sweeps a wider opening than a quarter turn.
WorkedExamples.Check: No measurement of line-arm length is used.

WorkedExamples.Title: A pair of equal angles
WorkedExamples.Question: Both angles describe two ray directions two compass eighth-turn intervals apart; one has longer printed arms. Are the openings equal?
WorkedExamples.Method: Count changes in direction, not the amount of printed ink.
Steps: Angle A has two equal compass intervals from its first ray to the second.
Angle B also spans two equal compass intervals.
The printed arm lengths differ, but neither angular opening does.
WorkedExamples.Check: Length variation does not change an angle's turn.

WorkedExamples.Title: Comparing described smaller compass openings
WorkedExamples.Question: Angle A points north and northeast; angle B points east and south. Which smaller angle is larger?
WorkedExamples.Method: Adjacent compass directions represent one eighth turn; east to south spans two eighth turns.
Steps: North to northeast is one compass direction step.
East to south is two compass direction steps.
The second opening is larger, without needing to draw or copy a publisher picture.
WorkedExamples.Check: A spans one eighth turn; B spans one quarter turn.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original 2021 Warm-up Which One Doesn't Belong (teacher-scored)
WorkedExamples.Question: Four original angle pictures: describe a mathematically valid reason why one angle doesn't belong, and give alternative criteria if possible.
WorkedExamples.Method: Inspect actual original source figures, compare angles' directions, shapes and openings.
Steps: For each figure, mark its vertex and arms if visible.
Choose a property that applies to a subset of the figures.
Defend the suggested exclusion and discuss alternatives with classmates.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Different mathematically defended exclusions may be valid; teacher checks actual source figures.
WorkedExamples.Check: Original figure descriptions are not reconstructed from an inaccessible image.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original Card Sort: at least three categories (teacher-scored)
WorkedExamples.Question: Sort the 2021 publisher angle cards into three or more meaningful angle-size categories and record a verbal label for each.
WorkedExamples.Method: Compare actual visual turn/opening, decide categories, justify borderline cases.
Steps: Inspect source cards only when legitimately available.
Group into three or more classes and explain the criteria.
Record each original source card identity in its category and justify to teacher.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Teacher-reviewed >=3 categories with actual card identity and reasoning.
WorkedExamples.Check: Numeric digital angle comparison does not demonstrate the source card sort.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original A–P Order Angles (teacher-scored)
WorkedExamples.Question: Place all original A–P angle cards in order from smallest to largest; explain why the extremes are smallest and largest.
WorkedExamples.Method: Align rays mentally or use permissible straightedges/tracing; compare openings rather than ray length.
Steps: Examine ALL 16 original A–P source cards on teacher-provided originals.
Order the observed openings; if any are equal, explain equality.
Teacher checks the actual ordered cards and student's explanation.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Depends on actual source cards, not invented digital degree values.
WorkedExamples.Check: No hidden publisher figure key or pixel parity has been asserted.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent first-party Cool-down
WorkedExamples.Question: Which is larger: a quarter-turn angle or a half-turn angle? How can you tell?
WorkedExamples.Method: Compare the amounts turned about the same type of vertex.
Steps: A quarter turn is one of four equal full-circle parts.
A half turn is two such parts.
Therefore a half-turn opening is larger; no longer rays are needed.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Half turn; the turning is twice a quarter turn.
WorkedExamples.Check: First-party equivalent assessment, not the original protected publisher Cool-down.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Thinking longer arms mean a larger angle.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The angle is defined by the direction change about the vertex, not the length of the rays shown.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Fix the directions while shortening or extending drawn rays; the opening stays equal.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Ordering the original A–P cards without inspecting all their illustrations.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: No source-card angle values or full ordering can be verified from the extracted teacher text alone.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher inspects each original card and hears a geometric justification for the ordering.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming one correct answer to Which One Doesn't Belong.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Several properties can support different legitimate exclusions.
CommonMistakes.Correction: State the geometrical attribute and explain why it separates the chosen figure from the others.

SummaryPoints: Angle size means amount of turn/opening, independent of arm lengths.
Original 2021 tasks: Which One Doesn't Belong, THREE OR MORE Card Sort categories, and complete A–P order with justification.
First-party digital pairs compare at most half-turn openings from named compass directions; they do not auto-grade protected original artwork.
The first-party quarter-turn/half-turn Cool-down requires an explanation; original publisher Cool-down remains unverified.
